question.text: Lotus Capital Cat II AIF wishes to add two external members to its Investment Committee whose names were NOT disclosed in the PPM at on-boarding. Under the SEBI (AIF) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2021, the appointment requires prior consent of what percentage of investors by value of investment?

answer.text: At least 75% by value of investment
At least 65% by value of investment

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Ch 11.7.3 (Investment Committee Approvals) and SEBI (AIF) (Second Amendment) Regulations 2021, external IC members whose names were NOT disclosed in the PPM/on-boarding agreement can be appointed only with consent of at least 75% of investors by value of investment. Disclosed external members and ex-officio members don't need this fresh consent. **The Trap:** 50% and 65% are lower thresholds that appear in other governance matters but not for IC external-member appointments. 100% is unnecessarily strict and not the regulation. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A tests the disclosure principle; XIX-C tests the specific 75% threshold, which is common in SEBI exam MCQs for Manager-governance. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Draft the PPM with a generous 'named-or-described' external IC bench so you never need 75% consent for a replacement — describe the role/profile, not just named persons.
